A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MAET and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The changed formatting and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original multilingual reasoning experiments, component ablations, out-of-domain evaluations, and the appendix's training-loss and parameter-similarity study.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds translated-data baseline comparisons and small-model experiments in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the language-model training input from ability-related to general corpus, and Section 4.2 replaces the stated dot-product implementation with cosine similarity. These are limited specification corrections: v1 already describes general-corpus training and cosine similarity elsewhere, so changes to the executed method are not established.

E1.justification: v2 adds GPT-4o-translated multilingual ability-related training corpora for new baselines. The evaluation tasks remain mathematical and scientific reasoning plus the retained supplementary tasks. Chinese remains represented in appendix experiments, and HumanEval remains explicitly discussed despite disappearing from its table.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds F-CPT_A, F-CPT_L&T, and F-CPT_T to the retained comparator set. The latter two introduce a substantive translated-data comparison family, testing an alternative way to obtain multilingual ability-related supervision that v1 did not evaluate in this comparison.

E3.justification: v2 adds RICER-based efficiency evaluation and experiments on Qwen2.5-0.5B and Gemma2-2B beyond the original LLaMA-3-8B setting. Table 2 changes from four-language to three-language averages. Retained training hyperparameters are unchanged; newly listed total token budgets do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds small-model generalization tests and a tensor-identification ablation. Figure 3's sensitivity results are revised, while Figure 2's component-ablation results and Appendix A's empirical study are retained. The tensor-specific analysis moves from Section 5.3/Table 3 to Appendix F/Table 8 without substantive change.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates for its experimental results.

E6.justification: v2 adds baseline, efficiency, and small-model result entries. Table 2 reports mathematical accuracy of 37.3 for F-CPT_L&T using 20B tokens and 35.7 for MAET using 12B. Shared per-language accuracies are unchanged apart from rounding; changed averages are not same-setting performance changes. Chinese comparator entries and the full HumanEval breakdown disappear, although some related evidence remains elsewhere.

T1.justification: Equation 1 specifies inverse-learning-rate scaling where v1 used an unspecified lambda factor. Table 2 also introduces a mathematical definition of token-based RICER, although its printed ratio conflicts with the reported values. The formal problem setup and decomposition/merging equations remain otherwise stable, with no new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract adds the quantitative claim of using 60% of computational resources, and the introduction changes the reported relative improvement from 9.1% to 10%. The central extraction-and-transfer contribution remains unchanged; the revised percentage accompanies different language averaging rather than improved shared per-language scores.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations attributing translation-baseline performance to translation quality and overfitting, and interprets small-model results as evidence of general applicability. It removes v1's LoRA-specific explanation and explicit limitations concerning broader cross-domain validation and continual-pretraining cost. Most existing mechanism and out-of-domain interpretations remain.

D1.justification: Table 5 newly discloses language coefficients: Spanish 1.5, Chinese 2.0, Bengali 1.2, and Telugu 1.2. v2 also supplies the translation prompt, per-method token totals, and hyperparameter-selection guidance. Existing learning-rate, batch-size, training-budget, and code/data-access information is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of MindMerger and LangBridge as related multilingual reasoning approaches, plus references supporting gradient selection, terminology, translation, and additional backbones. The original three-part related-work organization and overall research positioning remain.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the abstract and results discussion, removes the explicit contribution list, adds a concepts glossary, and moves implementation details and tensor analysis into appendices. Author ordering and terminology also change. Most prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The document changes from one-column to two-column layout. Table 1 is transposed, Table 2 gains grouped rows and efficiency columns, Figures 2 and 3 are rearranged, and the out-of-domain table switches to baseline scores plus colored differences. Algorithm 1 and tensor results move to appendices, which gain glossary and small-model tables.

improvement.justification: New translation baselines, small-model tests, and reproducibility details improve scrutiny of MAET. However, v2's blanket accuracy-superiority claim conflicts with Table 2's accuracy/cost tradeoff: F-CPT_L&T reports 37.3 using 20B tokens versus MAET's 35.7 using 12B. The new RICER formula also conflicts with its scores, and some result breakdowns disappear. These gains and reporting defects prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
